prompt: On signup, check whether a username is taken among 500 million users, answering most "it's free" cases without touching the database.
why: A Bloom filter says "definitely not taken" in memory; only "maybe" answers hit the database.
trap: Caching 500 million usernames costs far more memory than a filter's few bits each.

prompt: A web crawler must skip URLs it has already visited across billions of URLs, with tight memory and an occasional wrongly skipped page acceptable.
why: A small false-positive rate is fine here, and the filter fits billions of entries in a few GB.
trap: An exact set of billions of URLs would need far more memory.

prompt: A storage engine wastes time reading files on disk just to discover a key isn't in them.
tells: reading files on disk just to discover a key isn't in them
why: Keep a Bloom filter per file (as LSM trees do) and skip files that definitely lack the key.
trap: A cache helps with keys that exist and are hot, not with proving absence.

prompt: A news app must avoid recommending articles a user has already read, for 100 million users, using little memory per user.
why: A per-user Bloom filter of read articles: an occasional skipped article is a fine price.
trap: Storing full read histories for 100 million users is a lot of memory for a yes/no question.
